problem_statement: Cveinnt/LiveTerm is a runnable Next.js 12 + React 18 + Tailwind config-driven terminal-style developer portfolio: the home surface (src/pages/index.tsx) renders a wide ASCII LiveTerm banner and a command flow (help / about / projects / resume) driven by config.json, and there are two secondary terminal surfaces reachable at /projects and /stack. Design and ship a real PROJECT BROWSER on top of the terminal shell (src/components/ProjectBrowser.tsx): the developer's `projects` grid with its OWN 'filter by stack' control. A row of stack tabs (All / Rust / Go / TypeScript / Python) derived from the projects' own languages, when clicked, actually re-renders the project cards to the matching stack and updates a genuine result count (for example 'Showing 2 of 6 projects · Rust'). The browser is a shared component that stays continuous across the terminal: its tab row, count readout, and card grid appear on the home terminal AND on the /projects and /stack secondary terminal pages. Keep LiveTerm's own identity — the dark terminal ground with the Nord-green accent, the monospace type, the ASCII banner and the help/about/projects/resume command flow — so the browser reads as part of the same terminal, keeps its tab row and card grid within the 390px mobile viewport with no horizontal overflow, and emits no runtime console or network errors.
required_content: A real 'filter by stack' project browser (tabs All / Rust / Go / TypeScript / Python) sits above the terminal shell on the home surface; clicking a stack tab re-renders the project cards to the matching stack.
The browser shows a genuine result count that re-derives from the active filter (e.g. 'Showing all 6 projects' becomes 'Showing 2 of 6 projects · Rust' when the Rust tab is selected).

The project browser is a shared component and appears on the home terminal AND on the /projects and /stack secondary terminal pages (cross-page continuity); the full card grid renders on each surface.

The filter tab row and the filtered card grid stay within the 390px mobile viewport with no horizontal overflow and lay out cleanly (cards wrap into columns rather than spilling, overlapping, or clipping).

The browser adopts LiveTerm's own dark terminal ground and Nord-green accent, and the active tab is clearly legible (not dark-on-dark) — an on-brand terminal project browser, not an off-palette or broken control.

The existing terminal stays intact: the ASCII LiveTerm banner, the command prompt input, and the help/about/projects/resume command flow all continue to work alongside the new browser, and all captured states emit no runtime console or network errors.
design_constraints: Preserve LiveTerm's visual language: the dark terminal ground, the Nord-green accent, the monospace 'Hack' type, the bordered terminal container, the ASCII banner, and the interactive command prompt; the browser and its cards must adopt this same terminal identity.

Build the stack tabs from the projects' own language metadata, and render the shared browser so a single component covers the home, /projects, and /stack surfaces rather than duplicating markup per page.

The filter tab row must wrap or shrink and stay within the mobile viewport at 390px, and the filtered card grid must reflow into columns on narrow screens — do not pin the tabs to a fixed desktop width or force the cards into a fixed-width non-wrapping row that overflows a phone.

The result count and the visible card set must both re-derive from the live filter every render so they always match the selected tab; do not snapshot the grid or the count once and leave it stale when a tab is clicked.
Do not convert the site into a marketing landing page, blog, or dashboard; it stays a terminal-style developer portfolio with the home, /projects, and /stack surfaces.
Reuse the template's own local terminal styling and config; do not introduce external stock imagery, remote fonts, or live third-party API calls.
state_constraints: desktop_initial captures the home terminal at 1440px; the project browser panel is present above the ASCII banner and command prompt.
tablet_initial captures the same home terminal at 834px; the browser and grid stay readable.
mobile_initial captures the home terminal at 390px, where the browser's tab row and card grid MUST stay within the viewport with no horizontal overflow.
desktop_projects scrolls to the project browser and captures the stack-tab row, the result count, and the six project cards (All filter) laid out cleanly.
mobile_projects scrolls to the project browser at 390px and captures the tab row and card grid reflowed within the viewport.
desktop_projects_page captures the /projects secondary terminal surface; the shared project browser must also be present here (cross-page continuity).
desktop_stack_page captures the /stack secondary terminal surface; the shared project browser must also be present here (cross-page continuity).
desktop_help types 'help' into the prompt so the available-commands list renders in the terminal history; the browser and terminal shell stay intact.
desktop_filter_rust captures the browser after clicking the 'Rust' stack tab: the grid re-filters to the two Rust projects and the count updates to 'Showing 2 of 6 projects · Rust'.

change_completion: The terminal home surface has a working stack-filter project browser (All / Rust / Go / TypeScript / Python).
Clicking a stack tab re-renders the project cards to that stack and updates the result count to reflect it.
The ASCII LiveTerm banner, command prompt, and help/about/projects/resume flow remain intact alongside the browser.
The home, /projects, and /stack terminal surfaces stay reachable and render the terminal shell.
design_consistency: The browser and cards adopt LiveTerm's dark terminal ground and Nord-green accent, with a legible active tab.
The shared project browser rides home, /projects, and /stack continuously (tab row + count readout + card grid).
The terminal type, panel borders, and card language are preserved across the browser and the terminal shell.
regression: The 'help' command still renders the available-commands list in the terminal history.
The project browser appears on the /projects and /stack surfaces, not only on home, confirming cross-page continuity.
The ASCII banner and prompt input still render, and the Next build configuration and config.json are not broken.
responsive: 390px mobile home has no horizontal overflow; the browser tab row wraps/shrinks and stays within the viewport.
The filtered card grid reflows into columns on mobile without spilling, overlapping, or clipping.

author_notes: Repo-grounded Next.js 12 terminal-style portfolio task at L4 on Cveinnt/LiveTerm (LiveTerm), capability=Consistency, scope=cross_page. The graded change designs the terminal's OWN project browser: a stack-tab control (All / Rust / Go / TypeScript / Python) built from the project cards' language metadata that actually re-renders the cards and updates a real result count, shared across the home terminal and the /projects and /stack secondary terminal surfaces. Four orthogonal machine-checked gates: no_horizontal_overflow on the 390px mobile home (the tab row must wrap, not pin to a fixed/narrow desktop width); visual_regression on the browser-panel component crops at desktop_projects + mobile_projects (on-brand dark #262b36 ground + Nord green #a3be8c accent with a legible active tab and a clean card grid, not a broken overlapping grid with an illegible tab); cross-page dom_assertions that the browser (tpb__title 'Featured projects' + six tpb__card-name cards) rides /projects and /stack as well as home; and interaction_assertions that clicking the Rust tab re-filters the grid and updates the count to 'Showing 2 of 6 projects' (a snapshotted grid+count that never re-derives fails this). The baseline is the original layout defect (tab row pinned to a fixed 620px non-wrapping width, browser present on the home surface only) which fails overflow + visual + cross-page but passes interaction; the known-bad 'smart wrong' browser keeps a narrow non-wrapping off-layout tab row, breaks the filtered card grid into a single overflowing overlapping row with a dark-on-dark active tab, is home-only, and snapshots its grid and count at mount so the tab click succeeds but the terminal result stays stale, failing all four gates. INFRA fixes applied identically to all three legs (not part of the graded change): the upstream remote calls (api.github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, wttr.in, api.quotable.io) are replaced with stable local data so the terminal runtime is console/network clean, and the /projects and /stack secondary terminal pages are added so the cross-page continuity gate has real routes. The terminal's own monospace type, ASCII banner, and command flow are the local design assets reused as-is.
